title: Neural networks, side by side
describe: Runs one short sequence of words through different neural network architectures, all drawn the same way (time left to right, one column per word; depth bottom to top: input, hidden units, output), so they can be told apart by what each can see when a word goes in. Each hidden cell is banded in the colours of the words that sway it. `arch` is the one shown first: feedforward (no links between columns, so each answer comes from the current word alone: no memory), rnn (the hidden state is fed into the next step, so earlier words linger and fade; the last step says how far the first word has faded) or attention (each position looks straight back at every earlier word, weighted by relevance rather than distance). `compare` lists which architectures get a tab; switching tabs stays on the same word. With a one-word `sequence`, feedforward is a plain multilayer perceptron stepped through layer by layer (`layers` 1 to 3). Back / Next / Play controls. The activations and percentages are really computed from a small network with seeded made-up weights; `memory` (0 to 1.2) sets how strongly the RNN's state feeds back. Use it on cards about what a feedforward network, MLP or RNN is, how they differ, hidden state, sequence memory, fading memory over long sequences, or attention.

compare.description: Architectures that get a tab (default: all three; [] for no tabs)

sequence.description: The words fed in, one per step (default: The cat sat on the mat)

layers.description: Hidden layers in the feedforward network

memory.description: How strongly the RNN's state feeds back (0: none, so it behaves like the feedforward network)
